youtube.title: CAROLINE WHEELER
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke speaks with retired Nelson GP Dr Caroline Wheeler, recently censured by the Health Practitioners Disciplinary Tribunal for prescribing ivermectin during the pandemic. Caroline recounts why she felt compelled to treat desperate patients, the years-long disciplinary process that followed a colleague's complaint and the personal toll of fighting it while caring for her dying mother. She reflects on the broader campaign against dissenting doctors and urges others not to stay silent. For more information and to sign their declaration visit NZDSOS.com For news you can trust, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: BOTH BARRELS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke and Rachel Stewart discuss the fallout from Macklemore's pro-Palestinian protest during Ed Sheeran's tour, which saw Macklemore depart amid backlash from stadium owner Robert Kraft. The pair reflect on cancel culture's staying power, drawing parallels to their own experiences of professional ostracism and muse on luxury beliefs, the erosion of manners, and whether society is heading toward some larger reckoning. youtube.title: MONEY TALKS
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan talks with Farzin Irani of Sovereignty Capital about the Reserve Bank's expected interest rate hikes, which Farzin ties to currency defence rather than genuine economic strength. He walks through rising diesel costs, the widening gap between rich and poor and the geopolitical pressures building around Russia, Ukraine and Europe's economy, before turning to the scale of global sovereign debt and the risks lurking in bond markets. DISCLAIMER: The views and information shared on this show are for educational and informational purposes only. They do not constitute personalised financial, investment, tax, or legal advice. Listeners should seek guidance from a licensed financial professional who can provide advice based on their individual situation. For more information visit Farzin's new website Sovereignty.capital – with free resources to help people prepare for the future. Discover more from Farzin on Linktr.ee

youtube.title: LARRY BLAIR
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with energy policy commentator Larry Blair about the strained global fuel supply chain, as Houthi attacks near the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait and damage to Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline squeeze diesel exports to Europe. Larry explains why New Zealand's supply looks stable for now but remains vulnerable to price shocks, and discusses soaring shipping costs, potential US export restrictions, and the risks of further Middle East escalation. For the latest energy news get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: SAAD BAHJAT ABOU-CHAKRA
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with researcher and educator Saad Abou-Chakra about his open letter urging parliamentary candidates to clarify their foreign policy positions. Saad argues that selective media coverage skews public understanding of global crises, weighing New Zealand's nuclear-free stance and its role in Five Eyes against the risks of deeper military entanglement. He calls for greater scrutiny of candidates' worldliness and independent thinking ahead of the election. youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Foreign Minister Winston Peters about New Zealand First's health policy, which links diet and chronic disease to a wider critique of the medical system's reliance on pharmaceuticals. Peters points to vaping and reduced GST on whole foods as evidence for his approach, praises RFK Jr.'s health advocacy, and reflects on New Zealand's nuclear-free legacy and the shifting global security order. youtube.title: FIONA ANDERSON
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Fiona Anderson, manager of the Piha Campground, about the toll of its extended closure over flood risk. Fiona details her decades of on-the-ground safety measures, the conflicting flood models behind the council's decision and the near-4,000-signature petition backing her. She warns that forcing campers elsewhere will only push them into freedom camping outside residents' homes and questions why a single tragedy elsewhere should dictate Piha's fate. youtube.title: KEN TURNER
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan talks with Waitākere Ward Councillor Ken Turner about Auckland Council's push to close Piha Campground over flood risk. Ken argues the modelling behind the closure inflates future development scenarios to absurd levels, and questions whether liability concerns are driving the decision more than genuine safety. He warns that closing the campground would simply push freedom campers onto less-managed public land, with a local board decision looming this week.
